Reporting Times of the Tables, Predictions and Plots

Source: R/reporting_times.R
reporting_times.Rd

Returns the reporting times that write_survival_workbook and write_survival_report use, with their defaults filled in, so that tables, predictions and plots made with the other functions of the package can use the same times as the workbook and the report:

  • the spacing of the reporting times of the Kaplan-Meier tables, by default the spacing of the time axis of the plots of the data (the smallest of the usual intervals of the time unit, for months 1, 2, 3, 6, 12, 24, 60, 120 or 240, that gives at most 10 intervals up to the largest observed time);

  • the landmark times of the predicted survival, by default 6 months and 1, 2, 5 and 10 years in the time unit of the data (1 year = 365.25 days = 12 months), labelled "6 months", "1 year", "2 years", "5 years" and "10 years";

  • the time horizon of the extrapolation and of the restricted mean, by default the last landmark time.

Usage

reporting_times(x, interval = NULL, landmarks = NULL, time_horizon = NULL)

Arguments

x

Object returned by fit_survival_models.

interval

NULL (the default) or the spacing of the reporting times, a positive number in the time unit of the data.

landmarks

NULL (the default) or the landmark times, a vector of positive numbers in the time unit of the data. They are sorted and labelled with the time unit, for example "36 months".

time_horizon

NULL (the default) or the time horizon, a positive number in the time unit of the data.

Value

A list with interval (number), landmarks (data frame with the columns time and label), time_horizon (number) and time_unit (the time unit of x, for example "months").

Examples

dat <- processing_dataset(
  system.file("extdata", "fit_example.csv", package = "SurvFitSummary"),
  column_arm = "TRT01P", column_survtime = "AVAL", column_cnsr = "CNSR",
  control_arm = "Control"
)
fits <- fit_survival_models(dat, distributions = c("exp", "weibull"),
                            spline_scales = NULL)
times <- reporting_times(fits)
times
#> $interval
#> [1] 12
#> 
#> $landmarks
#>   time    label
#> 1    6 6 months
#> 2   12   1 year
#> 3   24  2 years
#> 4   60  5 years
#> 5  120 10 years
#> 
#> $time_horizon
#> [1] 120
#> 
#> $time_unit
#> [1] "months"
#> 
km_table(dat, interval = times$interval)
